messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate detected for customer Cobalt Systems (tenant cobalt-45) on dedicated pool dp-cobalt-1. 5xx spike ~32% for the last 5m. Paging on-call. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/cb/dp-pool-runbook
maya-oncall: on it. grabbing logs and checking pool health. ETA 2-3m.
dan-sre: I see CPU+OOM churn on nodes gp3-rt-6 in dp-cobalt-1, kernel oomkiller invoked twice. Could be a model change or a memory leak in runtime.
leo-eng-runtime: reverting any recent model config changes? There was a quantize rollout yesterday for redwood-owl-q2, but that was only for hosted. dp-cobalt-1 has a pinned variant: redwood-owl-dedicated-v1.
jess-cs: Heads up, Cobalt's support contact asked to be notified immediately. Their VPC peering shows no obvious network drop. They reported timeouts to our API and 500s.
maya-oncall: tagging @jess-cs to coordinate customer updates. dan, can you check tenant isolation? need to confirm other tenants on the same pool impacted.
dan-sre: checking tenant isolation now. `SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM requests WHERE pool='dp-cobalt-1' AND status>=500 AND ts>now()-interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY 1;` Results show 96% of 5xx from cobalt-45, small ripple (2-3%) from tenant cobalt-77.
leo-eng-runtime: if it's mostly cobalt-45, could be malformed KV cache growth for that tenant. I'm going to look at cache hit/miss rates and kvsize metric.
tara-eng-platform: I can spin up a short burst scale for dp-cobalt-1 (manual priority). Want me to add 2 nodes? That should reduce contention while we investigate.
amit-ops: go for it, do a quick scale + cordon/rotate suspected node gp3-rt-6. CMDs: ```redwoodctl pools scale --pool dp-cobalt-1 --add-nodes 2 && kubectl cordon gp3-rt-6 && kubectl drain gp3-rt-6 --ignore-daemonsets```
maya-oncall: scaling now. will monitor error rate.
incident-bot: ACTION: Manual scale started by tara-eng-platform. New nodes requested (2). Estimated attach time ~90s.
dan-sre: pulled runtime logs from gp3-rt-6: stack traces show repeated allocation failures inside attention cache resize during long-context requests. Repro rate higher when seq_len > 4096. Was there a sudden long-request surge?
jess-cs: Cobalt confirmed they were running a large batch eval earlier today that would have produced long contexts, they said it started ~30m before spike.
leo-eng-runtime: mitigation idea: enable per-tenant request size cap at the frontdoor for dp-cobalt-1 to prevent oversized KV growth while we patch. We can reject >8192 tokens with 429 and an explanatory header. Low blast radius.
dan-sre: also recommend temporary fallback routing: send cobalt-45 non-critical traffic to hosted fallback (redwood-owl-hosted-v1) where we can autoscale independently. That preserves critical SLA paths if they pick that option.
jess-cs: Cobalt's priority is availability for live API (not evals). I'll ask them if they can route evaluative batch work to a scheduled window. Suggest we offer hosted fallback for live endpoints.
maya-oncall: Implementing token cap and fallback routing now. Patch at edge config: ```edgectl set-limit --pool dp-cobalt-1 --tenant cobalt-45 --max-tokens 8192 && routingctl set-fallback --tenant cobalt-45 --target redwood-owl-hosted-v1 --percent 40``` Applying in 2m.
incident-bot: CONFIG APPLY: token cap + fallback ramp started by maya-oncall. Monitoring error rate and latency.
(2m pass)
maya-oncall: after scale + token cap + 40% fallback, 5xx dropped from 32% -> 6% in 5m window. Latency slightly higher for fallback requests but within SLA for interactive calls.
jess-cs: letting Cobalt know: draft update -> "We detected high memory pressure caused by oversized long-context requests within your dedicated pool. We applied a temporary token cap and routed a portion of traffic to our hosted fallback which reduced errors. We're coordinating options to avoid recurrence." Thoughts?
ana-exec: include impact summary and next steps: include rollback, runbook changes, and proposed credits per SLA. Exec needs a 1-paragraph summary + timeline.
leo-eng-runtime: immediate next step: patch runtime to prevent cache resize OOM by bounding pre-allocations and adding backpressure. I'll open a PR with a hotfix branch `runtime/limit-kv-prealloc` and target canary to dp-cobalt-1.
dan-sre: schedule canary after hours if risky; we should coordinate with Cobalt because of potential restarts.
jess-cs: Cobalt requests minimal disruption; they'd prefer fixes that don't require restarts. Offer an option: non-restart canary on hosted fallback + apply runtime param hotfix to dedicated pool with rolling restart window at 02:00 UTC.
maya-oncall: putting tasks in incident playbook. Quick action items: 1) Leo PR, 2) Tara schedule rolling restart, 3) Jess draft customer comms and credit proposal, 4) Dan prepare post-incident capacity review for dedicated pools. Assigning owners.
(10m later)
jess-cs: Draft to Cobalt (sending here for review): "Hi team, we experienced elevated error rates caused by unusually large context sizes in your dedicated pool. We reduced impact by scaling your pool, capping maximum tokens to 8192, and routing 40% of traffic to a hosted fallback. We're preparing a runtime patch and propose a goodwill credit for the SLA gap. Proposed next steps: schedule a maintenance window for a rolling restart (optional) and review best practices for batch/eval traffic. Can we set a call tomorrow?"
leo-eng-runtime: looks good. Add 'no customer data leak' confirmation (we checked logs; no cross-tenant leakage).
aman-ops: small typo: "we propose a goodwill credit" -> "we propose a goodwill credit equivalent to X hours of service at your committed rate". Fill X after we compute SLA window.
nana-exec: (typo in participants name corrected to ana-exec) Exec wants escalation doc by EOD with proposed credits and business impact. Jess, can you draft the exec note?
jess-cs: I'll prepare both the customer note and an exec brief. Will loop in finance for credit calc.
maya-oncall: marking incident as mitigated. Current 5xx steady at 2.1% (within tolerable ranges). Keeping page open for follow-up.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Total incident span so far: ~38 minutes.
leo-eng-runtime: creating PR: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/432 - hotfix limits prealloc & adds defensive OOM logs. Requesting review and canary to dp-cobalt-1.
dan-sre: once PR approved, we do a canary on a single node in dp-cobalt-1 during low traffic window. If stable 2 hours, roll.
jess-cs: customer comms scheduled; draft shared in #customer-updates channel. Propose 4 hours of service credit as initial offer; will confirm with finance.
maya-oncall: closing out immediate page. Post-incident tasks: RCA doc, runbook updates (add token size alerts + per-tenant kvsize metric), customer follow-up (exec summary + credits), dedicated pool capacity playbook.
jess-cs: thanks all. I'll own customer follow-ups and will ping when exec note ready.
nana-exec: thanks team, include a short bullet list for exec: root cause, mitigation, customer impact (duration, % requests), remedial actions, credit ask.
incident-bot: NOTE: Please add all follow-up artifacts to /incidents/1812345678 in the incident tracker. Reaction :eyes: to confirm.
